title: Prove the engine with a 1,000,000-hand invariant run
description:
As a project owner, I want a one-million-hand cash-game playtest covering every table size, so that I can trust the rules engine before anyone practises on it.

1,000,000 headless cash-game hands spread over all table sizes 2-10 with zero invariant violations, run on demand or nightly. Sit-and-go coverage of the 1,000,000-hand run is added in M3 by E05 (the sng level schedule is built there); bot line-up coverage by E06. At the permitted worst case (100,000 hands per 60 minutes) one million hands take about 10 hours, over the 6-hour limit of a GitHub-hosted job: the nightly run is sharded into parallel jobs (e.g. one per table size or 10 x 100,000-hand shards) each with a deterministic per-shard seed, or is run outside CI on the reference machine. Throughput: 100,000 6-max hands in at most 60 minutes on the reference machine (Apple-silicon Mac). Actor 'project owner' = the single Learner in the role of the person who builds and maintains the trainer (requirements.md has only the Learner user class).

## Requirements covered
- REQ-056 (Must): Reliability and invariants — The engine shall complete 1,000,000 headless hands across all table sizes, game types and line-ups with zero invariant violations, and the app shall recover from an unexpected error without losing completed hands.
- REQ-062 (Must): Headless playtest CLI — The project shall provide a command-line playtest runner that plays seeded bot-only hands with the production engine, checks invariants after every action and reports results.

Covers: REQ-056, REQ-062

## Notes
If sharding in CI proves impractical, run the 1,000,000 hands on the reference machine and attach the report to the story; E05 extends this run with sit-and-go hands in M3.

Plan key: E01-S17 · Dream: limit-holdem-trainer

nodes.title: Prove the engine with a 1,000,000-hand invariant run
Prove the game headlessly
Bootstrap the strict TypeScript project with one-command checks
Rank showdown hands by real poker hand rankings
Deal every hand from a seeded shuffle with a replay code
Play a complete fixed-limit hand from blinds to showdown
Give each deciding seat only its own view of the hand
Run seeded bot-only hands from the command line
Run every check in GitHub Actions on each push and pull request
Check game invariants after every playtest action
Let a short-stacked player call all-in
Split the pot into side pots for unequal all-ins
Play heads-up hands with heads-up blinds and order
Cap each street at one bet plus three raises
Reject illegal actions without changing the game
Allow short all-in bets and raises under the half-bet reopening rule
Show and muck cards at showdown in casino order
Move the button and blinds past busted seats
Play a sit-and-go
Prove the sit-and-go structure over the 1,000,000-hand invariant run
Face distinct opponents
Prove the engine over 1,000,000 cash hands with every line-up preset

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given an on-demand run of 1,000,000 cash-game hands spread over table sizes 2 to 10, When it completes, Then it reports zero invariant violations and exits 0 [REQ-056.2]

Given the CI workflow's nightly schedule or a manual dispatch, When the 1,000,000-hand run executes as parallel shards with deterministic per-shard seeds, Then every shard finishes within the 6-hour GitHub job limit, the combined report covers all 1,000,000 hands, and any invariant violation fails the workflow and prints the replay code and action history [REQ-056.2, REQ-062.2]
Given the same shard seed and options, When a shard is re-run, Then its output is byte-identical [REQ-062.4]
Given the reference machine, When `npm run playtest -- --hands 100000 --size 6` runs, Then it completes in at most 60 minutes [REQ-062.5]
Given a run split into shards, When results are combined, Then violationCounts are summed per invariant across shards and every shard uses the default checker
